# solo-msa_v2-gemini-3-8-flash-flash-ref

<!-- Generated by tools/export_results.py. Edit only the Experiment and Observations sections. -->

## Experiment

An exact repeat of [`solo` with the reference settings](../solo-msa_v2-gemini-3-8-flash-flash-saturation-medium-128k-vertex/summary.md) (`gemini-3.8-flash` on Vertex AI, `medium` thinking, 500 steps, compaction at 128K tokens, step counter, `$40` per-agent cost cap, 8 pairs at a time, 50-pair `flash` subset). Together with the [`coop --git` repeat](../coop-msa_v2-git-gemini-3-8-flash-flash-ref/summary.md), it measures how much the score moves by chance alone when nothing changes. The only planned difference is the time of day: the original ran in the evening, this one during US business hours.

One pair needed a restart. `pallets_click_task/2956` (1,8) stopped making progress after a dropped connection and a server error from the model API: for over 8 minutes the agent sent no requests and ran no commands. We stopped the run and resumed it under the same name, which kept the 49 finished pairs and reran only that pair from the start. The rerun used litellm 1.83.14 instead of 1.81.12; model pricing is the same in both versions.

## Observations

- 35/50 (70%) vs. 37/50 in the original run. Pair by pair, 48 pairs had the same outcome; 2 passed only in the original (`pallets_click_task/2800` (1,3) and `samuelcolvin_dirty_equals_task/43` (2,3)) and none only here. In both, one of the two features still passed.
- This matches the `coop --git` repeat (35 to 33, also 2 flips, both in the same direction). Across the two exact repeats, 4 of 100 pairs flipped and each score moved by 2, so differences of 2 or 3 pairs between single runs are within chance.
- The restarted pair passed, but took 336 steps and 134 minutes (150 steps and 75 minutes in the original), the longest pair in either run.
- Cost `$69.53` (`$1.39` per pair) vs. `$65.46`; the cost of the abandoned attempt of the restarted pair is not included. The wall time (135 min) and retry counts in the tables cover only the resumed part of the run; the whole run took about 8.5 hours, mostly waiting on the one long pair.
